subject: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: OmniHealth Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload

Hi Lina / OmniHealth procurement team —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a compact sizing + commercial note to help you decide between two deployment modes for the pilot: (A) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with VPC peering) or (B) Redwood Private (customer-managed private deployment). High level summary below, details in omni-pilot-sizing.xlsx.

TL;DR recommendations:
- Pilot target: 150 concurrent inference sessions (avg), peak 250 simultaneous streams; expected avg tokens/session ~4k; 99th percentile latency SLO 250ms.
- Option A (Dedicated): 6x H100-80GB-equivalent workers (in warm pool) + 1 head node; supports burst to 10 nodes. Estimated committed monthly cost (3 mo pilot) ~ $48k/mo. Lower onboarding friction, Redwood-managed security controls, VPC peering.
- Option B (Private): 4x H100-80GB on-prem + dedicated control plane + onboarding & ops support. One-time infra uplift ~ $220k (hardware + rack + network), monthly support/maintenance ~ $6k. Better data-residency, full isolation, but longer lead time (~6–8 weeks).

Tradeoffs we called out in the spreadsheet: util vs cost per token, cold start behavior, KV cache effectiveness (higher on Dedicated since we control co-location), audit evidence packaging (both supported; SOC2 artifacts available).

Asks from you:
1) Confirm pilot start window (we penciled May 17).
2) Which mode you prefer so we can finalize quote and reserve fleet if Dedicated.
3) Any procurement constraints (PO terms, vendor onboarding timeline).

I attached: omni-pilot-sizing.xlsx (sizing tabs + cost scenarios), omni-security-checklist.pdf, and a draft mutual action plan.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0122

From: OmniHealth Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>

Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@omnihealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop in our infra team:

1) For Option A (Dedicated): can you break out the monthly committed cost into: base compute, networking (egress), storage, and support? We need line items for our PO.
2) For the burst capacity you mention, is that billed only when used? Are there throttles if we hit region capacity limits?
3) For Option B (Private): do you provide a validated hardware BOM we can pass to our procurement? Any preferred vendor partners?

Also, we will need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short note on data retention controls for the pilot. Can you share the relevant docs?

If we can get answers by EOD tomorrow, we can confirm the May 17 pilot start.

Thanks —
Procurement Team (on behalf of Lina Park)
OmniHealth
procurement@omnihealth.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, OmniHealth Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload

Hi all — quick technical clarifications that might help procurement and infra: 

- Dedicated vs Private performance:
  * Latency: With Dedicated (co-located within Redwood fleet) we can guarantee p95 latency to the SLO via pre-warmed KV cache and colocated routing; Private depends on your on-prem network egress and will likely show 20–60ms higher median latency depending on network path.
  * Throughput: For sustained throughput it's about memory (KV cache) and batch windows. Our sizing assumes ~80% GPU utilization during business-hours with headroom for spikes.
- Burst billing: Dedicated burst is billed by node-hour when used. We include a small burst buffer in the pilot quote; additional burst beyond buffer is billed at on-demand rates.
- Hardware BOM for Private: attached is a proven configuration (H100 80GB or equivalent; dual 100Gbps NICs; NVMe-backed local). We recommend vendor partners: SuperMicro or Penguin Computing.

Operational notes: for pilots we configure a per-route routing policy that pins sensitive flows to isolated hardware; we can enforce egress-only to your VPC and provide audit logs (retention 90 days by default, extendable).

On SOC2/evidence: Vanessa — do you want me to pull the latest SOC2 package and redact internal-only pages?

Cheers,
Sergio
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: OmniHealth Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload

Lina / Procurement — thanks for the questions. Quick commercial notes to help your PO and internal approvals: 

- Detailed cost breakout (Committed Dedicated, monthly):
  * Base compute & runtime: $35,600/mo
  * Networking (VPC peering + egress buffer): $4,200/mo
  * Storage & snapshot retention (S3): $1,000/mo
  * Support & SRE on-call: $7,200/mo
  * Pilot discount applied: 10% off base compute for a 3-month pilot term.
- Burst: billed by node-hour beyond the included buffer; we can cap burst spend for the pilot if that helps approvals.
- Private (one-time + monthly): we can provide the BOM and qualified OEM quotes. Delivery and co-location take longer (4–8 weeks depending on vendor lead times).

If OmniHealth signs a 12‑month commit (Dedicated) we can improve pricing to ~20% off base compute and include a higher burst buffer. For the pilot I recommend Dedicated to reduce lead time and get you live faster; Private can be a follow-on if strict in-prem isolation is required.

Marissa — looping you for renewal/commercial lead input.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: OmniHealth Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing and commitment options for OmniHealth isolated workload

Lina — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per procurement asks: attached is a one-page cost breakout exported from the workbook (tab: COST-BREAKOUT). I also attached a redacted SOC2 summary and the hardware BOM for the Private path.

Next steps proposal: 
1) Confirm pilot start date (we still have May 17 open) and sign the attached mutual action plan.
2) If you choose Dedicated, we will reserve the warm pool and push a canned onboarding runbook (2 business days to get test traffic).
3) If you opt for Private, procurement signs the MPA and we start hardware order + install plan (estimated 5–7 weeks).

We are happy to cap burst spend for the pilot to avoid surprises — Lauren can put that in the MPA.

If you want, we can schedule a 30‑minute call tomorrow EMEA-friendly to run through the MPA and finalize PO language.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting OmniHealth started.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: omni-pilot-sizing.xlsx (see COST-BREAKOUT tab), omni-security-checklist.pdf, pilot-mutual-action-plan.docx
